title: Sparse-length quantizer batch allocator with KV-prefill awareness
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a new sparse-length quantizer batch allocator that reduces padding overhead and schedules KV-prefill-heavy requests earlier. Config flags are behind runtime.feature.sparse_length_quantizer and default to off for a controlled rollout.
description:
Motivation: production workload traces show a long-tailed sequence length distribution where naive fixed bucketing or uniform-width buckets cause excessive padding and poor kernel fit. Additionally, KV-prefill bursts (requests that attach large cached context) were causing spikes in prefill latency and unexpected KV cache thrashing. This PR implements a sparse-length quantizer allocator that (1) computes non-uniform bucket boundaries from recent traffic quantiles, (2) combines kernel-fit heuristics to prefer bucket boundaries aligned with efficient kernel shapes (e.g. 64/128 multiples for TensorCore lanes), and (3) integrates a lightweight KV-prefill awareness to prioritize or reserve prefill slots so continuous batching doesn't starve prefill-bound requests.

Implementation summary:
- allocator/service/runtime/sparse_length_quantizer.{cpp,h}: new allocator that maintains a sliding quantile summary (t-digest inspired) of sequence lengths with an EWMA window for drift. Quantiles are used to place incoming requests into a small number (configurable, default 8) of variable-width buckets.
- scheduler/kv_prefill_reservoir.{rs,cpp}: small reservation mechanism that marks N slots per batch for requests flagged as KV-prefill-heavy; integrates with continuous batching so prefill slots can be filled within a prefill_timeout window before normal batch composition proceeds.
- scheduler/batch_cost_model.{py,cpp}: extended cost model that estimates padding token overhead vs inferred kernel throughput; allocator chooses the bucket composition that minimizes expected cost = cpu+gpu_token_cost + padding_penalty.
- runtime/config.yaml: feature flag runtime.feature.sparse_length_quantizer and tuning knobs (num_buckets, quantile_decay_alpha, prefill_reserve_pct, prefill_timeout_ms).
- tests/unit/test_sparse_quantizer.py and tests/integration/test_prefill_reservation.py: exercise edge cases for skewed distributions and KV-prefill bursts.
- docs/running/allocators.md: operational notes and rollout steps.

Commits (high level): 1) add quantile summary and allocator core; 2) integrate with scheduler and cost model; 3) add KV-prefill reservoir and wiring; 4) unit + integration tests; 5) docs and feature flag. Changed areas: runtime/allocator, scheduler, runtime/kv_cache, runtime/config, tests, docs.

Example code snippet (high-level, illustrative): "if (is_prefill_heavy(req)) { reserve_slot = prefill_reservoir.claim(); if (reserve_slot) route_to_prefill_bucket(); } else { bucket = quantizer.assign(req.len); queue(bucket); }"

Performance results:
- Synthetic replay of customer trace A: 22% token-padding reduction vs current length-bucketing baseline, 9% lower p95 latency at 512-token tail workloads.
- End-to-end throughput improvement of 6-12% on p3dn-24 across mixed workloads due to better kernel fit.

Observability additions: new metrics: allocator.bucket_boundaries, allocator.padding_tokens_saved, prefill.reservations.used, prefill.wait_time_ms; dashboard panel in runtime -> batching to show quantile drift.

Backwards compatibility & rollout: feature is behind default-off flag and guarded; when enabled, allocator gracefully falls back to legacy fixed buckets on OOM or if quantile window insufficient.

Tests & CI: initial CI run failed (flake in integration prefill test due to timing), added deterministic timing hook and expanded wait time tolerance; all CI now passing.

Review thread (condensed):
- Owen Patel: "Great approach — concern about contention on quantile structure and GC pressure from per-request recording." Maya: "Quantile uses a compact reservoir sketch with batched updates every 50ms to avoid per-request allocations; added benchmarks showing <2% CPU. See commit 3 for batched_ingest optimization."
- Diego Alvarez: "What if kernel alignment heuristics cause worse packing for small models?" Maya: "Added cost model weighting to fall back to padding-minimizing composition when kernel throughput delta is small; added config knob kernel_alignment_weight (default 1.2)."
- Rina Sato: "Need to ensure prefill reservation can't be abused to starve normal traffic." Maya: "Prefill_reserve_pct defaults to 10% and is per-worker; reservations timeout (prefill_timeout_ms, default 30ms) and expire. Added metric prefill.reservations.expired and a test demonstrating fairness under burst."
- Requested changes were implemented in subsequent commits (batched quantile ingest, timeout guard, additional tests). Merge decision: after a short dogfood in staging for 48 hours and no regressions observed, approved and squashed.

CI summary: unit tests: pass, integration tests: pass, lint: pass, performance regression check: pass (no regression on p50/p95 for baseline scenarios).

Related: references ENG-8219 (dynamic batching improvements) and SUP-4191 (customer incident where KV-prefill bursts caused p95 spikes).

Notes for SRE: enable feature flag on canary pool using config runtime.feature.sparse_length_quantizer=true and monitor allocator.padding_tokens_saved and prefill.reservations.expired for 2 hours before wider roll-out.

Additional: included a small backwards-compatible API bump to scheduler metrics (added optional field "reservation_hint" to BatchEntry) — guarded in consumer code with feature flag.

notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: feature is off by default and includes multiple observability hooks and toggles to allow careful rollout across Dedicated and Private deployments.
